images.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Create ONE independent photorealistic rehabilitation exercise demonstration photograph, neutral starting position for seated active hip internal/external rotation.
Input images 1–3 are identity, wardrobe, hair, studio light and background references ONLY. Match the SAME adult East Asian woman, face and age impression, natural skin, body build, black ponytail, plain white short-sleeve fitted T shirt, dark charcoal gray long trousers. No need to copy the arm gestures.
Scene: seamless muted gray-blue studio backdrop and floor, soft diffuse studio lighting with natural shadows. Only a single sturdy unbranded straight-back dark gray chair with four widely planted legs, seat sufficiently high that BOTH BARE FEET hang freely several centimeters above the floor. This is a rehabilitation high chair, no wheels, no armrests, no footrest or crossbar under the shins, no wobbling. The thighs must rest on and be supported by the chair seat, their front ends level, almost horizontal; hips flexed about 90 degrees; knees flexed 90 degrees.
Pose s01: woman sits upright facing the camera, pelvis and torso level and centered, neutral relaxed expression, gaze forward. Knees at a comfortable fixed hip-width spacing. Both lower legs are vertical, ankles directly underneath their own knees. Bare feet hang with relaxed ankles, toes generally forward. Hands rest gently on the tops of each proximal thigh, away from kneecaps, without pushing. Do not spread the thighs widely, cross legs, point toes sideways or touch feet to floor.
Composition: portrait photograph approximately 1024x1536, true symmetric straight-on front view, camera at seated abdomen height, natural mid-telephoto proportions. Include full head, torso, pelvis, both knees, full shins and both full bare feet and all four chair ground contacts. Woman centered with moderate gray-blue margin and feet clearly floating above floor. Sharp clear anatomical joint connections and natural fingers/toes. Accurate body proportions.
No text, labels, numbers, arrows, watermarks, collage, split panels or diagram. Single pose only. Real photography, not drawing.

images.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational, precise rehabilitation pose photograph.
Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET and exact composition/identity/chair baseline. Images 2–4 are supporting references for the same woman's identity, white shirt, charcoal trousers, black ponytail and muted gray-blue studio photography.
Create one independent photograph by changing ONLY the woman's RIGHT lower leg (the lower leg on the LEFT side of the picture). Keep her head, face, torso, pelvis, hands, both thighs, both knee centers, left lower leg on picture-right, chair, light, camera and background exactly unchanged. Both thighs remain seated and supported, hips about 90 degrees flexed, knees about 90 degrees flexed and the same knee spacing as Image 1. Keep the right knee center at exactly its original image location.
Required s02 pose: seated RIGHT HIP INTERNAL ROTATION. From its neutral position underneath the fixed right knee, her right shin and ankle swing laterally OUTWARDS toward her own right side, which is picture LEFT. The right shin now makes a clear gentle diagonal descending from the FIXED picture-left knee toward picture-left ankle, about 25 degrees away from vertical. The entire lower leg changes direction together, not only the foot or ankle. The right foot remains connected naturally in line with the rotated lower leg, bare and completely visible. Her left shin on picture-right remains perfectly vertical and unchanged. Both feet hang freely above the floor, do not place either foot on the floor or chair.
Do not slide the right thigh sideways or lift the knee. Do not abduct the whole thigh, spread knees or turn the whole pelvis. No hand assistance or pushing. Natural comfortable endpoint.
Precisely preserve one-pose portrait 1024x1536 full figure frontal photograph, head and feet uncropped, all chair legs and their ground contact intact, same image scale. Preserve natural proportions, knee and ankle connections, skin and fingers/toes.
NO text, labels, numbers, arrows, watermarks, collage or split panels.
